solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Went with children to port (9)

blocks.note: wards are children in someone's care

annotation.surface: A parent takes the kids down to the harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: "Port" looks like a harbour town, but on a ship port is the left side, so "to port" means leftwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Sailors' jargon: port is the left-hand side of a vessel facing forward, so steering to port is turning that way.

entries.clue: Wolf born in bog (4)

indicators.note: B is placed in the bog, so the word for bog becomes the outer shell

blocks.note: loo = toilet, British slang for a bog
b. = born, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A wolf cub is delivered in a swamp.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bog" looks like a swamp, but it is British slang for a toilet, the same as loo.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional word: in the American Southwest the grey or timber wolf is called by its Spanish name.

entries.clue: How to get ready for holiday (7,8)

definitions.text: How to get ready for holiday

blocks.note: the surface means how to prepare; "ready" is also slang for cash, as in "the readies"
so the question is how you get cash to spend abroad

annotation.surface: Advice on packing and preparing before a trip abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ready" reads as prepared, but readies are banknotes: you get holiday money by foreign exchange.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful gloss: changing pounds into another currency at a bureau is the way to get spending cash for a trip.

entries.clue: Get bigger poster or flyer (7)

blocks.note: the moon waxes as it grows
a bill is a printed notice stuck on a wall

annotation.surface: Print shop advice: go for a bigger poster, or else a leaflet.
annotation.walkthrough: Next to "poster", "flyer" looks like a leaflet; it is a bird. A waxbill is a small African finch.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this small finch flies, and "flyer" is a loose, playful word for any bird.

entries.clue: Chef’s memory, for example (6)

blocks.note: RAM = random-access memory in a computer

annotation.surface: A cook's powers of recall held up as an example.
annotation.walkthrough: The "’s" reads as a possessive but is "is": the chef is memory plus for example. Gordon Ramsay is the famous shouty British TV chef.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Gordon Ramsay is one particular celebrity chef.

entries.clue: Woven cashmere (not a clue) (6,2)

indicators.note: threads woven together are rearranged into a new pattern

annotation.surface: A label on a jumper, with a sly aside that it gives nothing away.
annotation.walkthrough: The brackets look like the setter's aside, but "not a clue" is the definition: "Search me!" is what you say when you have no idea.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both are informal replies meaning you have no idea of the answer.

entries.clue: Trial partner in panic, wasting time (5)

indicators.note: to waste something is to use it up and lose it, so the time is lost from the word

annotation.surface: A co-defendant panics in the dock while the court's time slips away.
annotation.walkthrough: "Trial partner" sounds like a legal colleague, but it means the word paired with trial in "trial and error".
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase for learning by attempts pairs the two words, so each partners the other.

entries.clue: E for Einstein (7)

blocks.note: E is the first letter, the head, of EGG
the byword for a brainy intellectual

annotation.surface: A school report giving the great physicist a bottom grade.
annotation.walkthrough: E looks like a failing grade, which is a joke against Einstein. Read E literally instead: it is the egg's head.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the letter heading the word egg, and slang for an intellectual, of whom Einstein is the stock example.

entries.clue: That’s that! (8,7)

blocks.note: read as grammar: the word "that" is...
...a word class, the one "that" belongs to in "the book that I read"

annotation.surface: Someone closing a discussion firmly.
annotation.walkthrough: "That's that!" sounds like the end of an argument. Read it as a grammar lesson: that is a relative pronoun, as in "the book that I read".
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: "that" is one of the words, with who and which, that open a relative clause.

entries.clue: Edit what comes in? (6,4)

blocks.note: not a verb: this is what the answer, obeyed as an instruction, produces
the sea, as it comes in twice a day

annotation.surface: A newspaper editor asking which stories have arrived.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is an instruction that produces the clue. Make TIDE rise, reading it from the bottom of a down entry, and you get EDIT.
annotation.definitionFit: Two readings: the sea coming in, and an instruction to write a word upwards, which turns tide into edit.

entries.clue: Legal hurdle exposed by ten in the morning (3,4)

blocks.note: X is ten in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A law student's obstacle revealed at ten o'clock one morning.
annotation.walkthrough: The bar is the legal profession, and its exam is the test would-be lawyers pass, mainly in the US, to practise.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: the licensing test is an obstacle every would-be lawyer must clear.

entries.clue: A new setter joins us, showing some devotion (7)

blocks.note: gel sets hair, so it is a setter
us, as written, added on the end

annotation.surface: A new crossword setter joins the team and is loyal from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: "Setter" looks like the puzzle's author; it is hair gel. The Angelus is a Catholic prayer said morning, noon and evening.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: devotions are set prayers, and this Catholic prayer to the Incarnation is one of them.

entries.clue: Scientist saw reactions in liquid (3,5,6)

indicators.note: letters in a liquid are loose and float into new places

annotation.surface: A chemist watching things fizz in a test tube.
annotation.walkthrough: The "in" is shared: it belongs to the fodder and also starts the indicator "in liquid". Fittingly, Newton gave us the law that every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the English physicist behind the laws of motion and gravity is a famous scientist.

entries.clue: Chance of patient hugging short virgin (10)

indicators.note: a hug wraps one thing round another, so the patient goes round the virgin
something cut short is missing its end, so the virgin's word loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A hospital patient hugging someone with a slim chance of recovery.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chance" is used as an adjective, as in a chance meeting, not as a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical synonym: statisticians use the word for processes governed by chance, random ones.

entries.clue: Confusion is no good in story (6)

indicators.note: the no-good letters sit in the story, which wraps round them

annotation.surface: A reader complains that a muddled plot spoils the story.
annotation.walkthrough: "Is" looks like part of the sentence, but it just links the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a muddle of knotted thoughts or threads is a state of confusion.

entries.clue: A ludicrous tax to cage a bird (8)

indicators.note: a cage holds something inside it, so the phrase before it goes round the a

blocks.note: VAT = value added tax, the UK sales tax

annotation.surface: Someone protests a silly tax on keeping a pet bird.
annotation.walkthrough: The cage is the whole phrase "a ludicrous tax", and the caged letter sits where its two words meet. Few solvers know the bird, so trust the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this small red Asian finch, also called the red avadavat, is a bird.

entries.clue: One helping to hush up a report (8)

definitions.text: One helping to hush up a report

blocks.note: the surface suggests a fixer in a cover-up; the setter means a device that quietens
not a document but the bang of a gun being fired

annotation.surface: A fixer who helps bury an embarrassing report.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hush up a report" suggests a cover-up of a document; a report is also the bang of a gun, which a silencer muffles.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on report: the device screwed onto a gun barrel helps make the shot's bang quieter.

entries.clue: Firm kiss by lover, a keeper of course (8)

blocks.note: X = a kiss at the end of a letter
a swain is an old word for a lover

annotation.surface: A firm kiss from a sweetheart, the sort who is a keeper, of course.
annotation.walkthrough: "Of course" reads as "naturally"; here it means a boat's course. The coxswain steers a rowing boat and keeps it on course.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive gloss: the person steering a boat is the one who keeps it on its course.

entries.clue: Metal bolt and hammer (7)

blocks.note: wolf and bolt both mean eat greedily

annotation.surface: A metalworker's kit: a bolt and a hammer.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bolt" looks like hardware, but it means gulping food.
annotation.definitionFit: An older name: wolfram is tungsten, a hard metal, which is why tungsten's symbol is W.

entries.clue: Stand, fall, prepare for return (6)

indicators.note: something set up for return is ready to go back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: do = prepare, as in do the vegetables, turned round

annotation.surface: A list of commands, like stand up, fall down, get ready to come back.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stand" looks like a verb in a list of orders; it is a noun, a three-legged camera stand.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a kind of stand.

entries.clue: Awakening, we cooked parts of kidney (7)

indicators.note: cooking changes what goes in, so the letters of we are rearranged
to part something is to split it, and the cooked letters split the kidney word in two

annotation.surface: A cook wakes up to prepare a kidney dish.
annotation.walkthrough: "Parts" looks like pieces of kidney, but it is a verb: the cooked pair parts the kidney word.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a revival of interest or spirit, like a religious awakening, is a fresh start.

entries.clue: Leaving France, got attacked with acid (6)

indicators.note: France leaving means its letter departs from the word for got

blocks.note: F is the international car code for France

annotation.surface: A news story about someone who was attacked just as they left France.
annotation.walkthrough: "Got" means fetched, as in went and brought back, not simply obtained.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: printmakers mark metal plates by letting acid eat into the lines.

entries.clue: Clothes line and flapping tissue (8,6)

indicators.note: things flapping in the wind are thrown about

annotation.surface: Washing on a line, flapping in the wind, with a hankie among it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tissue" looks like one more item on the line; it is body tissue. The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscle to the heel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: tendons are bands of fibrous body tissue, and the heel's is the biggest.

entries.clue: Times will cut offensive words (4)

indicators.note: cutting into something puts you inside it

blocks.note: the Tet Offensive of the Vietnam War

annotation.surface: A newspaper promises to remove rude language.
annotation.walkthrough: "Times" looks like the newspaper and "offensive" like rude; one is the multiplication sign, the other the 1968 Tet Offensive. The definition is just "words".
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the written wording of a book or speech is its text.

entries.clue: Like some sex, or some instant rice (7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: lose the first three letters and the last one

annotation.surface: A comic choice between steamy sex and a quick microwave dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The two "some"s do different jobs: the first belongs to the definition, the second signals the letters inside "instant rice".
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive adjective: the slow, meditative sexual practice comes from Hindu and Buddhist tantra.

entries.clue: Why old ladies, say, will fill in (3,4)

blocks.note: the ladies is a public toilet, which is a WC

annotation.surface: A puzzled question about why elderly women step in to help.
annotation.walkthrough: "Old ladies" reads as elderly women, but it splits in two, and "ladies" is the women's toilet. "Fill in" is not one phrase either: "in" means at home.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal equivalent: asking how something came about is a casual way of asking why.

entries.clue: Best stuff to absorb energy (5)

indicators.note: a sponge absorbs water by taking it inside, so the energy goes inside the stuffing word

annotation.surface: An advert for a sports drink that soaks up energy.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stuff" is a verb, to cram, not a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the richest part rises to the top of milk, so it stands for the finest of anything.

entries.clue: As stated, studied map on alien world? (3,6)

indicators.note: something stated is said out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: read, past tense, is said like red
a plan is a map of a building or site

annotation.surface: Someone studies a chart of an alien world, as reported.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that "world" is defined by example: the answer is one particular world.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Mars, nicknamed for its rusty colour, is one world in the solar system.
